mechanism: A single local seed was judged against a DIFFERENT config's null distribution instead of its own config's replicates. war_eval_v1 read 22 lc = +3.16 sigma vs the vanilla-duck null (n=10, mean 15.20, sd 2.15) and was treated as a large local effect; it bought x1.00 on the public LB across 5 draws. Verified from the artifacts, war_eval v1/v2/v3 carry the IDENTICAL config label duck-harness-kaggle-warpack-v1 (same n_passes, same solver_label, three consecutive days) and are three SEEDS of one config: 22/15/13. Against its own replicates the headline seed is +1.13 sigma. The leaderboard was right; the single-seed read was wrong.
summary: Triggered by forum topic 736578 (local 5.0-5.4 -> LB 1.4, a 2.5x local gain buying zero), we tested local->LB transfer against our own record. Transfer is NOT the defect: large local effects have transferred (field-floor local x1.84 -> LB x1.70, ratios agree to 8%, baseline [INF]). The defect is single-seed reads. Within-config seed noise measured for the first time: vanilla sd 2.15 (n=10), warpack sd 4.73 (n=3), POOLED 2.80 lc. Our sealed +-5 lc single-seed bands are therefore 1.06-2.33 sigma (pooled 1.79 sigma, one-tail FP 3.7%), not the diff-SD 5.011 the preregs cite. Re-read against pooled sd: edge-1 -4.3 sigma (HARM stands), Arm 3 -3.6 sigma (stands), Arm A +0.7 sigma (NULL stands), edge-2's pending +-5 gate = 1.79 sigma, the weakest call we will have made.
lesson: Judge a seed against its own config's replicates, never against a different config's null. A single-seed SIGNAL of +5..+8 lc (<=~3 sigma pooled) is a DRAW, not a finding: it may head the queue (heading is nearly free under MAX scoring) but may not be recorded as a mechanism, entered in the registry as confirmed, or used to justify a follow-on build until a second seed reproduces it. Corollary: at 1.8 sigma per single seed, the marginal SEED buys more information than the marginal ARM.
